newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos has ordered the Central Bank to aggressively pursue its investigation on commercial banks engaged in manipulative foreign exchange trading (MANILA STANDARD/CHRONICLE/MALAYA)
- The decision to allow the peso to float means sad news for consumers as it will trigger a wave of price hikes in basic goods including petroleum products. (MANILA TIMES/INQUIRER)
- Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista mobilised governors and mayors to monitor prices of basic goods nationwide. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- A senator has asked Interior Secretary Robert Barbers to provide security to a Chinese-Filipino businessman suspected to be a drug lord. (INQUIRER)

- Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said he was optimistic the peso-dollar rate would stabilise in a few days. (MANILA BULLETIN) the peso by selling US dollars indirectly through selected banks, currency traders said. (MANILA TIMES)
- The Central Bank said it would maintain high interest rates to support its decision to allow the peso to float within a wider trading range. (INQUIRER)
- Central Bank governor gabriel Singson said the Bank will plug loopholes in currency transactions that speculators might have used against the peso in the past four months. (MALAYA)
